extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and authors seeking to discover or refine authorial, narrator, and character voice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on recognizing, creating, and sustaining voice at three levels (author, narrator, character) for prose and narrative fiction; includes constituent elements, quality criteria, development advice, and anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's recognizable signature across works (Hemingway, Atwood, Saunders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stable, cross-work signature: look for recurring choices in vocabulary, syntax, tone, worldview, and imagery that make an author recognizably theirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The voice telling this particular story (may differ from author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrator's phrasing, stance, and perspective are coherent for the story being told and distinct from the author's own voice when intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character voice
rubrics_metrics.description: How specific characters speak/think in dialogue and (sometimes) interior monologue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess individual characters for distinct diction, syntax, rhythm, and attitudes that make them believable and differentiated from other characters and the narrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: word choice, register, repeated words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze diction and lexical patterns: consistent register, favored words or phrases, and repeated lexical choices contribute to a recognizably voiced style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: sentence length, structure, rhythm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure sentence-level patterns (short vs. long sentences, clause patterns, parallelism) that create a rhythmic signature and affect readability and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: attitude toward subject (ironic, earnest, melancholic)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the prevailing emotional/coloring stance toward subjects and scenes; tone should align with content and desired reader response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view stance
rubrics_metrics.description: distance, sympathy, judgment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how the narrator or author positions themselves relative to characters and events — close or distant, sympathetic or judgmental — and whether that stance is consistent and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldview / sensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: what the writer finds important, funny, sad
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider recurring thematic emphases, values, and concerns that shape what the prose highlights; worldview often underpins voice and gives it thematic cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: recurring metaphors, sensory preferences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for favored metaphors, sensory registers (visual, tactile, olfactory), and image clusters that recur and form part of the writer's signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: how fast or slow the prose moves
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sentence/paragraph length, scene construction, and narrative momentum; pacing choices contribute to voice by controlling urgency and attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of silence
rubrics_metrics.description: what's left unsaid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate deliberate omissions, ellipses, and restraint — what the voice chooses not to state often shapes tone and reader inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive — recognizable on the page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should be identifiable and memorable; test by checking whether passages would be recognizable as from the same writer or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent — sustained across the work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should hold across scenes/chapters unless a deliberate shift is signaled; inconsistencies can confuse readers or weaken characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate — fits subject and form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice must suit the material (subject matter, genre, intended audience, and formal constraints); a mismatch undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earned — not affected or imitative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should arise from genuine engagement with the subject rather than feel forced, fashionable, or merely imitative of another writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audible (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audible — the prose has a sound you could read aloud
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test prose by reading aloud: voice should have a clear cadence, rhythm, and sonic quality that supports immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal (quality criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal — emerges from real engagement with the subject
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should reflect the writer's invested perspective, specific obsessions, and lived sensibility rather than generic commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read widely and notice what resonates
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Read widely and notice what resonates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to diverse voices helps you recognize patterns you admire or dislike; active reading (not passive consumption) informs your own choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a lot — voice emerges through volume
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Write a lot — voice emerges through volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular practice and producing many pages reveal recurring choices and help refine authentic voice; volume matters more than occasional brilliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust your obsessions
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Trust your obsessions — what you actually care about appears
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let subjects and concerns you return to naturally shape tone and focus; authentic interests often generate distinctive voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break rules consciously
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Break rules consciously — knowing when to deviate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn conventions first so deviations feel purposeful; deliberate rule-breaking can create a strong voice when tactically applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pastiche
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Avoid pastiche — imitation is a phase, not a goal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitating admired writers can be a learning step, but remaining in imitation prevents the emergence of a personal voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: How Voice Develops: Embrace specificity — generic voice = no voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific details, precise observations, and concrete images give voice uniqueness; vagueness flattens voice into generic prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop-bland voice (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Workshop-bland voice (no recognizable character)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid producing safe, neutral prose that reads like generic feedback-friendly writing; such 'workshop' voice lacks distinctiveness and fails to engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation / pastiche (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Imitation of one admired writer (pastiche)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While imitation may teach craft, relying on it long-term prevents development of an original voice and reads derivative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice over-tuned to genre conventions (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Voice over-tuned to genre conventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering slavishly to genre tropes can flatten individuality; balance genre expectations with personal specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice that fights the subject matter (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Voice that fights the subject matter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dissonant voice (tone or stance that resists the material) undermines authority and reader trust; voice should suit the subject's demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice inconsistent within a single work (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Voice inconsistent within a single work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexplained shifts in voice distract readers; ensure any changes in voice are motivated by plot, character, or formal strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice that draws attention to itself instead of the story (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-Pattern: Voice that draws attention to itself instead of the story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid self-conscious stylistic fireworks that showcase voice at the expense of narrative clarity; voice should serve the story, not overshadow it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saunders' definition: voice as style of speech + worldview
rubrics_metrics.description: "Voice is a particular style of speech, a way of putting things, a set of phrasings, tics, and cadences that suggest a particular mindset behind it." Voice and worldview are inseparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition as a diagnostic: look for phrasings, tics, cadences, and underlying mindset/worldview as the core of voice; assessing both form and content together yields the clearest sense of voice.
